spec.description: GPON ONT/SFP optical and network health: signal levels, temperature, voltage, bias current, ONU registration state, alarm flags, and interface error rates for on-call diagnosis.

spec.title: Transceiver Temperature (SFF-8472 DDM)
spec.description:
SFP module DDM temperature, not the SoC.
Internal calibration error is +/-3C
Commercial: 0 - 70C
Industrial: -40 - 85C

spec.title: ONU State
spec.description: ITU-T G.984.3 ONU operation states O1-O7; O5 (Operation) is the healthy in-service state

spec.title: Active Alarms
spec.description: Count of GPON alarm flags raised in the last 5 minutes. odi-oss reports los, lof and lom; the stock firmware also reports sf, sd, tx_mismatch and tx_too_long.

spec.title: GPON Alarms by type
spec.description: 1 = alarm raised at any point in the last 5m window, 0 = clear

spec.title: Stick CPU interface errors (/proc/net/dev -- CPU path only)
spec.description: gpon_network_* counts only traffic reaching the stick's own CPU (management, OMCI, DHCP...). User/service traffic is switched in hardware and never appears here -- use the Switch Port Drops / Port Hardware Errors panels for that. 32-bit counters, wrap at 4.29GB.

spec.title: Throughput (fibre & host side)
spec.description: rate(octets)*8 -- 64-bit counters, no wrap. port 2 = fibre/PON, port 0 = host (SFP cage). tx drawn negative.

spec.title: Stick CPU interface drops (/proc/net/dev -- CPU path only)
spec.description: Same CPU-only scope as the panel above; not representative of forwarded-traffic drops.

spec.title: Port Hardware Receive Errors
spec.description: Hardware port receive error rate by kind (crc_align, fragment, jabber, undersize), 64-bit counters. Undersize on port 3 (the CPU port) is one count per upstream OMCI reply: a 48-byte OMCI message plus FCS is a 52-byte frame, forwarded fine, and the stock firmware counts it the same way. It tracks how often the OLT polls, not a fault (OdiPortReceiveErrors ignores it). Oversize was removed in exporter v1.1.0 (ordinary 1519+ B VLAN-tagged traffic; see gpon_port_frames_total{size="1519_max"}).

spec.title: PON Optical Power (Rx/Tx)
spec.description: Class B+ RX: -8 (overload) to -28 dBm (sensitivity). TX: +0.5..+5 dBm. These are class B+ defaults, not the limits stored in the module: the module raises its own flags (gpon_transceiver_alarm). Hidden until ONU reaches O5 (registered) to exclude pre-registration bogus readings.

spec.title: HSGQ / ODI XPON SoC and GPON signal metrics

options.content:
# Common attenuation sources:

- **Upstream Length Loss:** `~0.5 dB` per Km on `1310 nm`.
- **Downstream Length Loss:** `~0.3 dB` per Km on `1490 nm`.
- **Splices Loss:** `~0.1 dB` per splice.
- **Connectors Loss:** `~0.6 dB` per connector.
- **Splitter Loss:** `log10(split:ratio) x 10 = Attenuation in dB` for each split.

Also see:
- [UISP Fiber: Designing a GPON Network](https://help.ui.com/hc/en-us/articles/115011654907-UISP-Fiber-Designing-a-GPON-Network)

- [Understanding GPON ONU registration states: Operation States 01 to 07](https://www.telecomate.com/mtk-solution-gpon-ont-onu-registration-process-and-omci-analysis)

- [Activation Process of ONU in EPON / GPON / XG-PON / NG-PON2 Networks](https://github.com/Strykar/GPON/blob/main/applsci-08-01934.pdf)

spec.title: SFP voltage
spec.description:
0 - 3.7 V, expects close to constant 3.3 V
Internal calibration: +/-3%

spec.title: OMCI Services
spec.description: Active OMCI service instances (gpon_omci_services). May be absent on a stick left on the OEM image/firmware.

spec.title: Uptime
spec.description: Seconds since last boot (/proc/uptime)

spec.title: Reboots (range)
spec.description: Counter resets of gpon_uptime_seconds over the dashboard time range = number of reboots

spec.title: Image / Firmware / Exporter
spec.description: gpon_image_info and gpon_exporter_build_info labels, joined by instance

spec.title: Exporter Health
spec.description: diag sections parsed/expected (equal = full scrape) and gpon_exporter_up

spec.title: ONU state over time
spec.description: G.984.3 state per stick; anything but O5 is an outage or a boot

spec.title: Frame-size distribution (fibre/PON, port 2)
spec.description: gpon_port_frames_total histogram, stacked by size bucket. New in exporter v1.1.1 -- may have no data yet.

spec.title: Pause frames
spec.description: gpon_port_pause_frames_total by port/direction (802.3x flow control)

spec.title: Switch Port Drops
spec.description: gpon_port_{receive,transmit}_drops_total by port -- the real forwarding-path drop counters (hardware-switched traffic never reaches the CPU, so /proc/net/dev drops below do not see it).

spec.title: Bias Current
spec.description: Internal calibration: +/-10%

spec.title: Memory
spec.description: gpon_memory_bytes by kind; used = total - free - cached - buffers

spec.title: Load averages
spec.description: gpon_load{1,5,15}. On odi-oss the load sits near 0 at idle. On the stock firmware it is pinned at 2.00 (the watchdog and led_swBlink kernel threads sleep in D state), so do not alert on it there.

spec.title: PON Optical Power Trend (Tx/Rx)
spec.description: Hidden until ONU reaches O5 (registered) to exclude pre-registration bogus readings

spec.title: FEC in use
spec.description: 1 when FEC is in use in that direction (ds: the OLT sends it, us: the ONU sends it). Off with a healthy fibre means the OLT port runs without FEC; a weak line then shows as BIP errors instead of FEC corrections.

spec.title: ONU-ID
spec.description: The ONU-ID the OLT assigned in ranging. It changes when the OLT re-registers the ONU.

spec.title: Upstream grants/s
spec.description: BWmap allocations accepted for this ONU, per second, over the rate interval. How many a second is the OLT's choice (about 500/s on one OLT, about 2,000/s on two others), so compare with this stick's usual rate. 0 while the ONU says O5 means the OLT stopped granting it upstream time (a stuck ONU).

spec.title: Counter samples/s
spec.description: How often the driver read the GPON line counters; one per second is normal. Anything else means the sampler is stalled and every counter in this row is stale or low.

spec.title: Saturated samples (range)
spec.description: Samples in the selected range where a 16-bit hardware counter read full: that second lost counts, so rates in this row undercount. Expected 0.

spec.title: FEC codewords/s
spec.description: Downstream FEC codewords per second. corrected: the line is noisy and FEC is repairing it (a weak line at -32 dBm showed about 25k/s). uncorrectable: data is lost; any sustained value is a real fault. Hardware counters, sampled once a second by the odi-oss driver.

spec.title: Bit error rate (estimate)
spec.description: Estimate: FEC-corrected bits per second divided by the downstream line rate, 2.48832e9 bit/s. It counts only errors FEC repaired, so it understates the true BER once uncorrectable codewords appear, and it reads 0 when downstream FEC is off (see FEC in use): then the BIP-8 line is the signal. The BIP-8 line is bit errors the BIP-8 check found per bit of downstream (the basis of SF and SD, G.984.3 11.1.3), after FEC when FEC is on. Not a calibrated measurement.

spec.title: BIP-8 errors/s
spec.description: Downstream BIP-8 errors per second: blocks (what the ONU reports to the OLT in REI) and bits. The line takes errors even if FEC hides them from the payload.

spec.title: Upstream grants: BWmap allocations/s
spec.description: BWmap allocations accepted for this ONU per second: the OLT granting it upstream time. How many a second is the OLT's choice (about 500/s on one OLT, about 2,000/s on two others): compare with this stick's usual rate. 0 while the ONU state says O5 is a stuck ONU: ranged and registered but the OLT stopped granting, so nothing goes upstream (check gpon_us_bursts_total too). Far above this stick's usual rate (about 9x was seen after a power cut on one line) means the OLT sent a garbage or oversized bandwidth map: look at gpon_ds_bwmap_errors_total and re-register the ONU. Allocation errors by kind are shown on the second query.

spec.title: LOS/LOF/LOM events
spec.description: Times each alarm was raised in each interval: LOS loss of signal (no light, fibre pulled), LOF loss of frame, LOM loss of PLOAM message. Read every 100 ms while activated, so a shorter loss can be missed.

spec.title: LOS/LOF/LOM seconds in alarm
spec.description: Seconds each alarm was asserted in each interval.

spec.title: ONU state transitions
spec.description: State changes per interval, by state left and entered. A fibre pull shows as O5 to O6 to O1; repeated O5 to O6 flaps point to a marginal link.

spec.title: PLOAM, REI and timers
spec.description: PLOAM messages the driver handled per second (ds received from the OLT, us sent), REI messages sent per second, and TO1 (ranging) / TO2 (POPUP) activation timer expiries per second.

spec.title: Downstream GEM frames/s
spec.description: GEM frames per second by kind. idle frames fill unused downstream capacity; non_idle carry data. Both are 32-bit hardware counters over the whole downstream, not only this ONU's frames: a fully idle 2.48832 Gbit/s downstream is about 62 million idle frames a second (a 5-byte idle frame each, measured on one line, not read from the stock firmware), so idle x 5 x 8 / 2.48832e9 is the idle share of the downstream capacity. A count that stops growing at 4294967295/s would be saturation (see Saturated samples).

spec.title: Downstream GEM errors/s
spec.description: GEM errors per second by kind, and HEC errors the GEM block corrected. Expected near 0; a rise next to FEC corrections is the same weak line seen one layer up.

spec.title: OMCI frames/s
spec.description: Downstream OMCI messages the GEM block received per second: the OLT managing the ONU. Bursts of activity are normal at registration and after provisioning changes.

spec.title: Upstream bursts and GEM frames/s
spec.description: Upstream bursts the ONU sent and upstream GEM frames per second. Bursts at 0 while grants are present, or while the ONU is in O5, means the ONU is not transmitting.

spec.title: Upstream GEM bytes/s
spec.description: Upstream GEM bytes per second, including the 5-byte GEM headers. A 32-bit hardware count that does not fill at line rate.

spec.title: Uncorrectable FEC blocks (range)
spec.description: FEC codewords the line could not repair over the selected range: data was lost. Expected 0.

spec.title: LOS events (range)
spec.description: Times loss of signal (no light, fibre pulled) was raised over the selected range. Expected 0.

spec.title: Line errors/s
spec.description: Downstream line errors per second. FEC corrected: the line is noisy and FEC is repairing it. FEC uncorrectable: data is lost, any sustained value is a real fault. BIP error blocks: what the ONU reports to the OLT in REI; the line takes them even if FEC hides the errors from the payload. Detail per counter is on the GPON link detail tab.

spec.title: Upstream grants/s
spec.description: BWmap allocations accepted for this ONU per second: the OLT granting it upstream time. How many a second is the OLT's choice (about 500/s on one OLT, about 2,000/s on two others): compare with this stick's usual rate. 0 while the ONU state says O5 is a stuck ONU: ranged and registered but the OLT stopped granting, so nothing goes upstream (check gpon_us_bursts_total too). Far above this stick's usual rate (about 9x was seen after a power cut on one line) means the OLT sent a garbage or oversized bandwidth map: look at gpon_ds_bwmap_errors_total (on the GPON link detail tab) and re-register the ONU.

spec.title: Link events
spec.description: Times each alarm was raised (LOS loss of signal, LOF loss of frame, LOM loss of PLOAM message) and ONU state changes, per interval. A fibre pull shows as O5 to O6 to O1; repeated O5 to O6 flaps point to a marginal link. Alarms are read every 100 ms while activated, so a shorter loss can be missed.

spec.title: GEM bytes/s per port, downstream
spec.description: Per GEM port, bytes per second including the 5-byte GEM headers. A port that went silent while the others move drops to 0 (the table shows the last value). Ports that are provisioned but unused stay at 0.

spec.title: GEM bytes/s per port, upstream
spec.description: Per GEM port, bytes per second including the 5-byte GEM headers. A port that went silent while the others move drops to 0 (the table shows the last value). Ports that are provisioned but unused stay at 0.

spec.title: GEM frames/s per port, downstream
spec.description: Per GEM port, GEM frames per second. A port that went silent while the others move drops to 0 (the table shows the last value). Ports that are provisioned but unused stay at 0.

spec.title: GEM frames/s per port, upstream
spec.description: Per GEM port, GEM frames per second. A port that went silent while the others move drops to 0 (the table shows the last value). Ports that are provisioned but unused stay at 0.

spec.title: Upstream GEM frames vs Ethernet frames
spec.description: All GEM ports of a stick: GEM frames sent upstream against Ethernet frames sent upstream. More GEM frames than Ethernet frames means the Ethernet frames are fragmented into several GEM frames; the two lines together mean no fragmentation.

spec.title: GEM flow count faults (range)
spec.description: Per-flow counts the driver could not read in time (ack_timeout) or read full (saturated), in the selected range, summed over both kinds. Stays 0; any increase means the per-GEM-port rates above under-count. n/a: the image does not export the per-GEM-port series.

spec.title: Host port auto-negotiation: running vs stored setting
spec.description: state=running: what the host port does this boot (blue = on = negotiates 1000BASE-X with the host, off = forced 1000BASE-X full duplex, purple = off). state=setting: the stored HOST_AUTONEG (on, or unset / off). A running line that differs from the setting line is the boot fallback. n/a (blank): the image does not export it.

spec.title: Host link up
spec.description: Whether the stick's host port has link with the host (1 = up). n/a: the image does not export it.

spec.title: Host port: fallback, trial and boot watch
spec.description: fallback: HOST_AUTONEG is off but this boot found no link forced and runs auto-negotiation (red while it holds, green = none). trial: a keep-or-revert trial of the mode is running (blue while it runs; it reverts by itself unless confirmed). watch: the boot watch is still deciding the mode (blue while it runs, up to 10 minutes after a boot with the key off; gray = no). n/a (blank): the image does not export them.

spec.title: Safe-mode boot
spec.description: 1 when this boot is a safe-mode boot: the PON off, the host port on auto-negotiation and the default password in force for that boot only. Red when 1. n/a: the image has no safe mode (nothing exported).

spec.title: Safe-mode record unacknowledged
spec.description: 1 while the record of a safe-mode boot waits to be acknowledged (it may have cleared HOST_AUTONEG). Red when 1. n/a: the image has no safe mode (nothing exported).

spec.title: GPON stats
